description: Trigger evals for graphql-contract-review: it reviews a proposed GraphQL schema or BFF contract before any code exists, while its siblings handle REST contracts, post-implementation risk review, consistency sweeps, and whole-system design.

should_trigger: Can you look over the SDL I put in the plan for the new checkout subgraph before we start building it? I am worried about the nullable fields.

We are adding a BFF for the mobile app that stitches orders, loyalty points and shipping status into one screen payload. Nothing is coded yet. Check the contract in IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md and tell me if it holds up.

Draft schema for the product catalog is in DECISIONS.md. Products have variants, variants have prices, and the list field takes a plain page number and limit. Is that going to hurt us once clients depend on it?
Our federated graph is getting a new inventory subgraph and I am not sure who should own the Product entity. Review the proposed design before anyone writes resolvers.
Before we lock this design: the web BFF will hold the refresh token in localStorage and call the payments service with it. Sanity check the GraphQL side of the plan.

should_not_trigger.prompt: I sketched the new REST endpoints for invoices: POST /invoices, GET /invoices/{id}, with a 409 on duplicates. Check naming, pagination and idempotency before we implement.
The GraphQL resolvers for the orders subgraph are already merged on this branch. Review the diff for correctness and safety problems before I close the slice.
The schema and resolvers are all written now. Run the defect-class pass over the code for convention drift and missing tenant checks before I package the PR.
We are thinking about splitting the web app into micro-frontends with one team per section. Should we adopt that, and what would the boundaries look like?
The new endpoint takes a user-supplied redirect URL and returns account data. Do a threat model and an ASVS pass on the change I just finished.
